translation_notes: prefixes: rdf, sh. The draft also declared rdfs, never used here: removed. `import ldpy` added for ldpy.ANY.

THE finding of the region: `graph.remove((ps, SH.path, path))` is run when `path = graph.value(ps, SH.path)` is None (a property shape without sh:path), and rdflib reads that None as a wildcard (it removes nothing, since the shape has no sh:path). `-{ {ps} sh:path {path} }` raises TypeError there (an interpolated None never matches silently). The faithful form is `-{ {ps} sh:path {ldpy.ANY if path is None else path} }`: the wildcard that arrives as data is ldpy.ANY, per the reference. Not a literal `-{ {ps} sh:path ?p }`: that would remove EVERY sh:path of a shape, where the original removes the one g.value returned (the fixture has a shape with two sh:path values; the mutant fails). This is the one site of the stratum with a None: the other 7 removals are fully bound.

Reads: `graph.objects(None, SH.property)` -> `m{ [] sh:property ?ps }`; `graph.subjects(RDF.type, C)` -> `m{ ?ps a C }`; `graph.objects(ps, P)` -> `m{ {ps} P ?o }`; `graph.value(ps, SH.path)` -> `m{ {ps} sh:path ?path }.first()` (value() takes the first, no cardinality check); `graph.triples((ps, dctsource, None))` with the unpacking `_, _, o` -> `m{ {ps} {dctsource} ?o }`. The mutations of the graph inside these loops (remove of the very triple being walked) behave the same in both.

`dctsource = <http://purl.org/dc/terms/source>` stays a Python variable holding an IRI (it is then interpolated as `{dctsource}` in term position, predicate included): turning it into `dcterms:source` would delete a variable of the original.

Kept as Python: `graph.items(o)`, `Collection(graph, o)`, `collection.clear()` (RDF list traversal and clearing: no island for a collection), and every `BNode()` (a `_:{}` blank node is a function of its data, not a fresh node). Not folded: the `first`/`rest` pairs separated by `next_b = BNode()` (folding would move the BNode() call; the pairs that follow each other, `first`+`rest rdf:nil`, are one `;` island). The two adds `(ns, sh:property, shapes[0])` and `(shapes[0], sh:path, path)` are one two-statement `+{ }`.

`@graph graph` designates the parameter; the nested `add_or_shape` function uses `+{ }` and sees the enclosing designation (no `nonlocal` needed). Prefix bindings: sh and rdf are added to the caller's graph without overwriting; harness green.
No shim: rdflib's SH, Collection and collections are real.

Driver: whole fixture (merge of three shapes on a path with sh:in overlap, sh:or on nodeKind/datatype/class, a lone shape, a shape without sh:path, a shape with two sh:path values, a node shape with no property shapes, an orphan property shape, stray neighbours), a graph with no node shape, a graph with only the shape without sh:path. The sets in_values/nodeKinds are walked to build RDF lists: only IRIs and literals go in them, so the order is the same on both sides (each forked from the driver). Mutants killed: `{path}` (TypeError), `?x` for the removed path (two-path shape loses its second path), `-{ ?z {dctsource} {o} }` (needs a source shared between two shapes: srcShared on nameB and ageShape). Equivalent mutant, noted: `-{ {ps} sh:datatype ?x }` (all datatypes of ps are in the loop's set and go anyway).
